findings.reason: without the split, the node's record of which arms are red at base is wrong for two of its three arms, and its gate cannot tell a preserved behaviour arm from a failing-first one.
findings.text: s34 requires every new test to fail at the base revision, then states two arms that pass at base by construction: "A tracked crew.json deleted from the working tree without a commit is still refused, naming the file, as it is at the base revision" and "Promoting a run the store already holds is still refused as a duplicate in both states"; the base revision already refuses both (reckon/ledger.py:3778 refuses the uncommitted deletion naming the path, and the duplicate refusal precedes it), so a worker reading the sentence literally must either manufacture a red arm for an arm the section says holds, or record an arm as failing that cannot — the same defect earlier reviews had moved out of s32's and s31's failing-at-base sentences

findings.reason: the declared depends-on edge gates §26 until s34 is declared done and f-hpdw-013 introduces no batch dispatch, so the stale sentence costs a reader a moment of confusion, not a wrong dispatch.
findings.text: the still-open followup f-hpdw-013 states "§26 waits on §21 to §25, §28 and §29" and names §22 as its next build, but every one of those is declared done (plan.html:28) and §26 now also waits on s34 (plan.html:29); a coordinator reading that body would dispatch §26 without §34

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — docs/state/reckon/crew.json and docs/state/reckon/runs resolve and are tracked at the base revision; the mechanism s34's Why blames exists at reckon/ledger.py:3692 ("its absence is a deletion to recover") and the refusal it produces at reckon/ledger.py:3778; the cited run and its all_debug job 1322899 resolve in that run's manifest.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s34's "New tests, each failing at the base revision" (plan.html:431) covers three arms, two of which the same sentence fixes as still holding at base.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate logs s34 names go under a crew run directory, and the run it cites for its evidence resolves at ~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261115T211459261234-untracking-migration-s26/ with post-untracking-promotion.log and reproduce_untracking.sh already there.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s34 names no plan label, stage name or ticket number; its prose describes the mechanism (an absent ledger that git history still records) rather than pointing at a tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence (the reproduction log prints POST_UNTRACKING_PROMOTION_REFUSED with rows_before and rows_after both 2 and canonical_rows_preserved true, and ledger.py's `_ledger_ever_tracked` asks git log --all, which still finds the path after a committed git rm), and the failing arm it names is obtainable and can fail, the two preserved-behaviour arms being the ones the done_when finding covers.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s34 delivers one endpoint, a promotion landing after a committed removal of the ledger while an uncommitted deletion still refuses; the preserved-behaviour arms are controls on that one endpoint, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan-section-depends-on (plan.html:29) now carries s34 as an upstream of s26, and the open followup f-hpdw-015 (plan.html:515) queues §34 before §26 resumes; s34 needs no upstream of its own because its done-when runs over a temporary repository and store, not over the real migration.
